summary: Tested estimate approval + deposit end to end (backend + UI + real Stripe test checkout). Almost everything works. The deposit % input defaults to 25, a 30% estimate saves and the card shows '30% deposit', Send shows a toast and the badge becomes 'sent'. On the public page, approve-btn stays disabled until the signature has 2+ chars AND the box is checked, and after approving the approved-badge + deposit-box ($900 for $3,000 at 30%) appear and persist on reload. The existing token page showed 'signed by Dana Approver' / 'Pay $1,350.00 deposit'. Paying with 4242 card on checkout.stripe.com redirected back with session_id, polling turned it into the deposit-paid box, the URL param was cleared, the owner card badge reads 'deposit paid', and the bell shows both 'approved estimate' and 'Deposit of $1,350.00 received' (only one deposit notification). Public API: unknown token 404, deposit before approve 400, approve twice returns the same signature/approved_at, 0% deposit 400, 1-char signature 422, unknown session 404, send with no email 400. PUT on an approved estimate keeps status approved, the signature and the token. Regression: estimate edit/delete OK, Jobs crew modal OK. Found 1 real bug: re-sending an approved or paid estimate resets its status to 'sent'.

critical.issue: Always $sets status='sent'. Re-sending an approved (or deposit-paid) estimate downgrades it to 'sent'. The public page then shows the Approve box again, and the customer can re-approve, which overwrites signature_name/approved_at/signer_ip and adds a duplicate notification. The Send button is still shown on approved/paid cards. Reproduced in test_estimate_approval.py::test_full_flow.

minor.issue: deposit_amount is always recomputed from the current total*pct. The stored deposit_amount (actually paid) is ignored. If the owner edits line items or deposit % after payment, the 'Deposit of $X received' box shows the wrong amount. Use est['deposit_amount'] when deposit_paid.

The owner can change line items, total or deposit % after the customer e-signed (and after the deposit was paid) with no warning or re-approval. The signed scope no longer matches. Consider locking it, or resetting the approval when pricing changes.

A new Stripe session is created on every click, so a customer with two tabs can pay twice (the second _fulfil_payment is skipped but the card is still charged). origin_url comes from the client unvalidated and is used for success/cancel URLs (open redirect). Use FRONTEND_URL or whitelist it.

Fulfilment runs whether or not this request actually flipped the row to paid. The deposit_paid check is a separate read, so concurrent polls/webhook can race into duplicate notifications. Only fulfil when update_one.modified_count == 1.
min_length is checked before strip(), so ' a' passes and is stored as 'a' (1 char).

ui_bugs.issue: The Send button is enabled on approved/deposit-paid estimates (triggers the status reset bug). Hide it or relabel it 'Resend link' without changing status.
The 'Deposit received — thank you!' toast shows twice after the redirect (StrictMode double effect; the cancelled flag doesn't stop the in-flight first poll). Dev only, cosmetic.
Line-item desc/qty/price inputs and the remove X have no data-testid.

issues: Checkout showed EUR (€1,252.77) as the default currency, with USD as an option (Stripe adaptive pricing based on location). Consider turning off adaptive pricing if you want USD only.

action_items: HIGH: In send_estimate, don't overwrite status when it is 'approved' (or deposit_paid), e.g. only set status='sent' if the current status is draft/sent. Hide/relabel Send on approved cards.
Show the stored deposit_amount after payment. Consider locking pricing edits after approval.
Validate origin_url (use FRONTEND_URL). Reuse an open deposit session or block a second payment.
Make fulfilment idempotent via modified_count. Strip the signature before validating its length.
critical_code_review_comments: _public_estimate recomputes deposit_amount instead of using the paid amount.
Notifications for deleted estimates stay (orphan estimate_id).
server.py is 1347 lines; estimates/public/payments should be split into routers.

success_rate.backend: 95% (1 of 7 new tests failed, a real bug; the full suite is 80/85 with 4 flaky crew/audit failures that pass on a solo rerun because of parallel-run data contention)
